title: AIBAST Agents Library — roadmap
subtitle: What is shipped, what is in flight, and what is deliberately parked.
note: Status here is what the repository can demonstrate, not what is planned. An item is Shipped only when a gate or a live URL proves it.

lanes.label: Shipped
lanes.blurb: Provable today — a gate, a test, or a live page.

items.title: 112-agent industry library
items.detail: Single-file agents across 14 industries, each with a manifest, a one-pager, an architecture and a machine review.

items.title: FY27 priority agents
items.detail: Seven agents consolidated from 61 customer-named variants; six FY27 clusters dropped as already covered and two merged.

items.title: PowerPoint export, not printed PDF
items.detail: Every one-pager and architecture exports native editable slides built from the same static data the page renders.

items.title: Media served off a branch
items.detail: Demo recordings live on the media-server branch and stream into the site, so they are never in the install clone.
items.evidence: media.js · depth-1 clone measured 3.7 MB .git vs 2.6 GB

items.title: Shallow install
items.detail: install.sh and install.ps1 clone at depth 1; only version pinning deepens, because a tag needs history to resolve.

items.title: No customer data, enforced
items.detail: A denylist gate sweeps every tracked and untracked text file. It caught its own documentation naming an organisation.

lanes.label: In flight
lanes.blurb: Working, not finished. Named with what is still missing.

items.title: Video engagement
items.detail: Plays, likes and comments per demo, using GitHub Discussions as the backend so nothing needs a server. Threads are not seeded yet, so every count reads zero.

items.title: Generated demo films
items.detail: Seven films pass the showcase gate at 159-164s with a neural voice. They are not published: the automation still needs a pass before these sit beside the professional recordings.

items.title: Domain b-roll
items.detail: No footage exists for HR or editorial scenarios, so those films borrow cross-industry footage and say so rather than pretending it argues the scenario.

items.title: Duplicate film projects
items.detail: Ten projects were built from the raw un-consolidated FY27 names and duplicate agents that shipped under consolidated ones. Left in place rather than deleted.

items.title: RAPPedia
items.detail: The library's own encyclopedia: every agent, pattern, decision and term as a linked note, built from what the repository already knows rather than written separately. Sixteen brain notes and a graph exist under api/v1/brain; what is missing is the reading surface, search, and the link from each agent to the concepts it uses.

lanes.label: Parked
lanes.blurb: Deliberately not being worked on, with the reason.

items.title: RAPPVision compositing pipeline
items.detail: Composited our content onto the professional cut. Archived: the last render passed all 16 of its own gates and an independent frame-by-frame review still returned NOT RELEASABLE.

items.title: Live-action capture
items.detail: No original filming. The library uses the recordings it already has and generates the rest.

items.title: Publishing generated films externally
items.detail: Held until the generated cuts are indistinguishable from the professional ones. Shipping a visibly weaker cut devalues the recordings that are not weak.

items.title: RAPPedia authoring by hand
items.detail: Notes are derived from manifests, decisions and gates. Hand-written encyclopedia entries would drift from the code the moment they were written, which is the failure this library exists to avoid.

principles: An item is Shipped only when a gate or a live URL proves it.
A known flaw named is fine; one a customer finds is not.
No figure the product cannot stand behind reaches a customer surface.
Large media lives on a branch, never in the clone.
